title: Elastic Buffer Pools, Predictive Prewarm, and Tenant Isolation Contracts — Dedicated Capacity PRD
creator: Aisha Patel
overview: This PRD defines Elastic Buffer Pools, a predictive prewarm system, and Tenant Isolation Contracts for Redwood Dedicated. The goal is to provide deterministic latency and graceful burst handling for reserved customers while protecting isolation guarantees and reducing cost of idle reserved capacity.
problem_statement: Customers on Dedicated capacity experience two recurring problems: (1) sudden short-lived bursts cause tail latency spikes or request rejections because reserved GPUs are cold or saturated, and (2) overly conservative headroom reserved for guests increases cost. Current fallback strategies (regional fallback, lower-tier models) preserve availability but degrade customer experience. We need a solution that smooths transient spikes, reduces cold-starts, and enforces tenant isolation SLAs without permanently inflating reserved commitments.
goals: Provide an Elastic Buffer Pool abstraction that preserves tenant isolation while allowing short-term absorbtion of burst traffic.
Implement Predictive Prewarm to reduce cold-start token latency for reserved pools using lightweight workload signatures and recent traffic heuristics.
Define Tenant Isolation Contracts (TICs) — explicit, machine-readable contracts that dictate isolation class, burst entitlement, preemption behavior, and observability expectations.
Expose operator controls for buffer sizing, burst backstop limits, and per-tenant billing signals in Redwood Console.
Ensure end-to-end SLO compliance: <100ms median and <350ms p95 token latency for reserved pools under normal load; predictable degraded mode under burst scenarios.
non_goals: Replace existing long-term reservation/commit models or commit to multi-day capacity changes; this is focused on short-term burst and warmup behavior.
Implement deep model-level reconfiguration or on-the-fly quantization as part of prewarm — kernel/runtime improvements remain engineering scope but out of this PRD.
Change pricing model for reserved contracts in this initiative (billing UX will surface metrics but pricing changes require separate approval).
scope_included: API surface for creating and configuring Elastic Buffer Pools attached to reserved capacity slots.
Predictive Prewarm engine that recommends and triggers warm instances or lightweight cached KV prefixes based on traffic signals and tenant policies.
Tenant Isolation Contracts schema, validation, and enforcement hooks in the scheduler.
Console UI surfaces for buffer diagnostics, burst ledger, and manual override controls for SRE/SEs.
Acceptance tests and synthetic workloads for verifying SLOs and isolation behaviors.
scope_excluded: Payment/billing change flows for customers based on buffer usage.
Major infra refactors (eg full scheduler rewrite) — integrate with current scheduler extension points.
Public SDK changes (non-necessary) — only administrative APIs and telemetry will be added.
requirements:
Functional requirements:
1) Elastic Buffer Pools (EBP): create/attach an EBP resource to a dedicated reservation. EBPs must accept short-lived queued tokens up to a configurable cap, expose utilization metrics, and only be used for burst-level requests that match tenancy policy.
2) Predictive Prewarm: system must analyze last 1h and 24h traffic histograms and issue prewarm actions when probability of burst > X% (configurable default 10%). Prewarm actions include: spin a lightweight worker process, pre-load top-k KV cache entries, or provision temporary fractional-GPU containers.
3) Tenant Isolation Contracts: schema (JSON) listing isolation_class (strict|balanced|opportunistic), burst_entitlement (tokens/sec or tokens/60s), preemption_policy (soft|hard), and audit_url. Contracts validated at reservation binding time.
4) Fallback & Billing Signals: when EBP is exhausted, scheduler must route to configured fallback (lower-tier model or regional fallback). EBP consumption recorded to tenant ledger for later invoicing/alerts.
Non-functional requirements:
1) No change to control plane latency > 50ms p95 for normal reservation operations.
2) Predictive Prewarm decision pipeline must complete <200ms for each decision tick.
3) All telemetry must be exported to existing console/tracing backends with per-tenant and per-buffer aggregation.
4) Backwards-compatible — tenants without TICs should default to isolation_class balanced and have no EBP attached.
acceptance_criteria: Create an Elastic Buffer Pool via admin API and bind it to an existing reservation — API returns 201 and buffer id.
Simulated burst (10x baseline QPS for 12s) is absorbed by EBP in 90% of test runs with p95 token latency <= 350ms and no request rejections until buffer exhausts.
Predictive Prewarm reduces cold-start median token latency by >= 40% for a cohort of synthetic start-of-session spikes compared to control.
Tenant Isolation Contract rejected when invalid fields or higher-than-allowed burst_entitlement are specified — validation tests pass.
When EBP exhausted, requests are routed to configured fallback and fallback metrics increment appropriately; no silent request drops.
Console displays buffer utilization, recent prewarm actions, and a per-tenant burst ledger within 60s of events.
SRE oncall runbook updated with playbook steps for buffer overuse, prewarm failures, and manual revoke of EBP capacity.
Automated regression tests cover scheduler enforcement, predictive prewarm decision logic, and telemetry emission.
success_metrics: Reduction in customer-observed p95 cold-start token latency for Dedicated reserved customers by 30% within 90 days of rollout.
Decrease in emergency fallbacks (customers routed to hosted) for reserved pools by 50% under short bursts.
Operational cost delta: targeted increase in short-term bursting infra spend <5% vs baseline while reducing SLA incidents.
Adoption: >= 25% of new reserved contracts opt-in to EBPs/TICs within first quarter after GA.
constraints: Must interoperate with current scheduler extension points and not require changes to tenant binding flow.
Predictive signals are limited to telemetry we currently ingest (recent request counts, model variant, token length distributions) — no new expensive traces.
Budget: initial implementation must fit into next quarter engineering allocation for Dedicated infra (approx 4 FTE-weeks of infra work + 3 FTE-weeks frontend).
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (internal alpha): feature flags for EBPs + TICs enabled for internal tenants and SRE — run synthetic soak tests (2 weeks).
Phase 1 (limited beta): opt-in for 10 strategic customers with engineering support; collect telemetry and refine thresholds (4 weeks).
Phase 2 (wider beta): enable in console for self-serve opt-in; surface cost signals and warnings (6 weeks).
Phase 3 (GA): default TICs for new reservations available, EBPs visible in reservation settings, doc and runbook published.
engineering_notes: Scheduler: add EBP token accounting hook — tokens consumed first from reservation, then EBP until cap.
Telemetry: add new metrics: ebp.utilization, ebp.prewarm_count, ebp.exhaust_events tagged by tenant.
Prewarm: lightweight heuristic service runs every 10s making binary prewarm/no-prewarm decisions per reservation.
Storage: burst ledger is append-only for auditability; retention policy 90d then rollup to monthly aggregates.
Rollback: feature flag to immediately disable EBP usage at cluster level and drain outstanding prewarm workers.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Prewarm causes wasteful infra spin-ups and increases cost. Mitigation: conservative default threshold (10%), cost cap per-hour per-tenant, and opt-in requirement during beta.
Risk: EBPs weaken isolation and allow noisy tenants to impact others. Mitigation: enforce TICs strictly in scheduler and include per-tenant backpressure and soft-preemption hooks.
Risk: Complexity increases operator burden. Mitigation: Console summaries, alerts for abnormal consumption, and SRE playbook.
open_questions: What is the default burst_entitlement unit (tokens/sec vs tokens/60s) that balances billing observability and scheduler simplicity?
Should predictive prewarm be throttled by budget vs accuracy? Who owns the budget control UX?
How to model EBP usage in long-term billing without breaking reserved contract guarantees? Should it be invoiced as overage or reconciled monthly?
next_steps: Product: finalize TIC schema with privacy/compliance review (2 weeks).
Eng: prototype EBP token accounting in testcluster and add telemetry hooks (3 weeks).
Design: deliver console mockups for EBP summary and manual buffer override (2 weeks).
Customer Success: recruit 6-10 beta customers and prepare onboarding materials (4 weeks).
